Gov. Kathy Hochul’s artful dodge on the issue tells you all you need to know: She’s going to give Mayor Zohran Mamdani at least some of his tax hikes — next year, once she’s safely re-elected.

This year, she sent him some state money and OK’d some dodgy new borrowing, then pushed through his pied-à-terre tax; asked outright this week if she’ll give him more next year as a reward for his support now, she offered only a coy “There are no quid pro quos,” conspicuously saying nothing about taxes but pointedly saying she looks forward “to continue working in partnership” with the mayor on matters of mutual interest.

Until now, the gov has sworn up, down and backward to oppose increasing taxes on the rich.

“This is not an austerity budget, but it is a disciplined one,” she announced in January at the unveiling of her spending plan, boasting that she was “protecting taxpayers.”

In July she thundered, “We should not be raising taxes on high-net-worth individuals,” or “on the companies that are creating the jobs and generating the revenue that helps us pay for the services that people in New York City come to rely on.”

Not that any of that boasting stopped her from breaking her word and pushing through the pied-à-terre tax.

And now even that pantomime of prudence is out the window; she didn’t  even wait until the day after the election to start backpedaling.

For readers who don’t speak Albanyese, “continue working in partnership” means  Mamdani’s getting his way.

Don’t forget Hochul’s history of writing postdated checks on closed accounts.

Even before her pied-à-terre reversal, she delivered a congestion-toll bait-and-switch.

In mid-2022, just in time for her last gov election, she halted the congestion tolls, saying she wanted to give the feds and the public more time to review the program.

Then, having secured another four years, she turned the tolls back on — even claiming she was doing everyone a favor by starting them off at $9, not more.

Oh, and never mind the broken promise about the tolls reducing traffic for more than a brief period.

Similarly, Hochul this year pressed “pause” on her green agenda, giving the impression she’s won’t knuckle under to anti-progress fruitcakes.

And she won’t — until Election Day is safely past.

Most important, don’t fool yourself: A vote for Hochul is now a vote to empower Mamdani and his dream of statewide tax hikes to fund his New York City spending agenda.

You can still vote to derail that train, saving New York from the inevitable boiler explosion of high taxes and economic ruination.

Vote Blakeman, or rue the consequences.

بیشتر پوشش ما را در نتایج جستجوی خود ببینید.Gov. طفره رفتن ماهرانه کتی هوچول در مورد این موضوع همه آنچه را که باید بدانید به شما می گوید: او حداقل برخی از افزایش مالیات شهردار زهران ممدانی را در سال آینده، پس از انتخاب مجدد، به شهردار خواهد داد. در این سال، او مقداری پول دولتی برای او ارسال کرد و مقداری قرض جدید و ناموفق گرفت، سپس از مالیات سرپایی او گذشت. این هفته به صراحت از او پرسید که آیا او در سال آینده به عنوان پاداشی برای حمایت‌اش در حال حاضر به او می‌دهد یا خیر، او فقط با تعجب گفت: «هیچ پولی وجود ندارد»، آشکارا چیزی در مورد مالیات‌ها نمی‌گوید، اما به وضوح گفت که مشتاق است «به همکاری با شهردار در موضوعات مورد علاقه دوجانبه ادامه دهد». تا به حال، دولت سوگند یاد کرده است تا با افزایش مالیات بر ثروتمندان مخالفت کند. او در ژانویه در مراسم رونمایی از برنامه هزینه‌های خود اعلام کرد: «این یک بودجه ریاضتی نیست، بلکه یک بودجه منظم است. او در ماه جولای گفت: «ما نباید مالیات افراد با ارزش خالص بالا را افزایش دهیم» یا «بر شرکت‌هایی که شغل ایجاد می‌کنند و درآمدی ایجاد می‌کنند که به ما کمک می‌کند تا برای خدماتی که مردم شهر نیویورک به آن تکیه می‌کنند پرداخت کنیم».
نه این که هیچ کدام از آن لاف زدن او را از شکستن قولش و فشار دادن به مالیات بردار بازدارد. و اکنون حتی آن پانتومیم احتیاط از پنجره بیرون است. او حتی تا روز بعد از انتخابات صبر نکرد تا شروع به عقب زدن کند.

Former House Speaker Nancy Pelosi, D-Calif., criticized New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani and Michigan Democratic US Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed over their views on Israel Thursday, calling their positions “wrong” and saying they did not reflect congressional Democrats.

The two progressive Democrats were mentioned by “On Brand” podcast host Donny Deutsch, who asked Pelosi how he, as a Jewish man, could reconcile his support for the Democratic Party with politicians whose statements he considered antisemitic.

“When you say Israel doesn’t have the right to be a Jewish state, that’s antisemitic as far as I’m concerned with all that,” Deutsch said.

When Pelosi asked for examples, Deutsch named Mamdani and El-Sayed, calling their comments “concerning.”

“No, it’s more than concerning,” Pelosi responded. “It’s wrong. It’s wrong. And it isn’t a reflection of the Democrats in the Congress of the United States. This new person in Michigan, we’ll see if he gets elected to the Congress.

“But the mayor, bless his heart, I hope he succeeds as mayor, but I don’t agree with some of the things he has said. But in terms of our people in the House of Representatives, if somebody says that, the other members disassociate themselves from it.”

Before he was elected New York City mayor, Mamdani repeatedly dodged questions when asked if Israel should be a Jewish state. In a June 28 interview with ABC News, however, Mamdani said he supported Israel as a state with equal rights but declined to endorse it as a Jewish state.

“I think any state that privileges one religion over the other is one that I can’t tell you I support, whether it be Israel or Saudi Arabia or anywhere else,” Mamdani said.

El-Sayed has repeatedly declined to affirm whether Israel has the right to exist as a Jewish state.

In a May appearance with Jewish supporters, the candidate said he “struggled” to answer this question and suggested the idea of a Jewish state wasn’t consistent with the liberal values “we say we believe in here in the United States.”

Earlier in the interview with Deutsch, Pelosi initially denied that anyone in the Democratic Party was antisemitic.

“The fact is that I really do not know of anybody there on our side who is engaged in antisemitism. That may be what it appears to be or what they’re charged to be. But if they are, it’s only a few. If there are, I think sometimes they say things that they shouldn’t and can be interpreted that way,” Pelosi said.

Despite her concerns about Mamdani and El-Sayed’s comments, she dismissed their impact on the party as a whole.

“People represent their districts, and we have to respect that. The job description, job title is representative, but that doesn’t mean it has an impact on the consensus of the Democratic Party, and [House Minority Leader] Hakeem Jeffries has been very clear on that,” Pelosi said.

Rabbi Yaakov Menken, executive vice president of the Coalition for Jewish Values, acknowledged Pelosi “as one of the Jewish community’s best friends among House Democrats” but said it was alarming that she did not seem to recognize antisemitism among her colleagues.

“Pelosi claims she wants for those voices to be marginalized within her party, yet she demonstrates that she has turned a deaf ear, both to antisemitic expression from her colleagues and to the rabbis anxious to set her straight on the magnitude of the problem,” Menken told Fox News Digital.

“If she is indeed one of our best friends, should we not be scared by that?”
news.content:
پوشش ما را در نتایج جستجوی خود مشاهده کنید. نانسی پلوسی، رئیس پیشین مجلس نمایندگان، زهران ممدانی، شهردار نیویورک و عبدالالسید، نامزد دموکرات سنای آمریکا در میشیگان را در مورد دیدگاه‌هایشان در مورد اسرائیل در روز پنجشنبه مورد انتقاد قرار داد و مواضع آنها را "اشتباه" خواند و گفت که آنها منعکس کننده دموکرات‌های کنگره نیستند. دو دموکرات مترقی توسط دونی دویچ، مجری پادکست «آن برند» نام برد و از پلوسی پرسید که چگونه می تواند به عنوان یک مرد یهودی، حمایت خود از حزب دموکرات را با سیاستمدارانی که اظهاراتشان را یهودی ستیزانه می دانست، هماهنگ کند. هنگامی که پلوسی برای مثال درخواست کرد، دویچ از ممدانی و السید نام برد و نظرات آنها را "نگران کننده" خواند.
پلوسی در پاسخ گفت: «نه، این بیش از آن نگران کننده است. "این اشتباه است. اشتباه است. و بازتابی از دموکرات ها در کنگره ایالات متحده نیست. این فرد جدید در میشیگان، خواهیم دید که آیا او برای کنگره انتخاب می شود یا خیر." "اما شهردار، قلبش را رحمت کند، امیدوارم به عنوان شهردار موفق شود، اما من با برخی از مواردی که گفته است موافق نیستم. اما در مورد مردم ما در مجلس نمایندگان، اگر کسی این را بگوید، سایر اعضا خود را از آن جدا می کنند."
ممدانی قبل از انتخاب شدن به عنوان شهردار نیویورک، مکرراً در پاسخ به این سؤال که آیا اسرائیل باید یک کشور یهودی باشد، طفره می رفت. با این حال، ممدانی در مصاحبه ای در 28 ژوئن با ABC News گفت که حمایت می کند

A Canadian real estate CEO and his two daughters were shot while his wife was struck with a hammer during an invasion inside their multi-million-dollar home in an affluent Toronto neighborhood Thursday morning.

MAC Group boss David Morton and his family were attacked when three masked men stormed into their gated Bridle Path property at around 3:45 a.m., according to The Toronto Sun.

The suspects, who were armed with handguns and a hammer, gained access to the five-bedroom residence through a back door, Toronto Police Service Inspector Kristy Smith told reporters.

Morton, 75, and his daughters, Maggie Zohil-Morton and Cristina Zohil-Morton, confronted the unidentified intruders who were wearing ski masks and hoodies inside the home.

“A struggle ensued during this altercation in which the suspects fired their guns multiple times and one victim was struck with a hammer,” Smith said.

The trio “tried to fight off” the trespassers when they were shot, sources told the outlet.

Morton and one of his daughters were shot in the leg, while the other daughter suffered a gunshot wound under her arm, the outlet reported.

Morton’s wife, Doriana Zohil-Morton, who also serves as the president of the MAC Group, was attacked by one of the hammer-wielding suspects.

Two of the family members suffered “life-altering injuries” and remained hospitalized while the other two sustained non-life-threatening wounds, Smith said.

The family members were not identified by their injuries.

Descriptions of the suspects were not revealed, but officials said they had fled the area in an SUV.

It was not immediately known if anything was stolen from the house during the invasion.

A motive for the attack was not revealed but it is believed they were looking to rob the upscale neighborhood.

“There was a violent interaction. There was a demand made for valuables from within the home. Whether or not they escaped with anything is uncertain at this point,” Smith said.

“An affluent area where people would have things that are sought after would be the motivation for this,” Smith added.

The 5+1 bed, 7 bath is valued at $2.1 million and includes a tennis court, in-ground pool and private gardens to “enhance a luxury lifestyle” according to an online listing.

A nearby home on 10,000 square feet of property is listed for $8.45 million in the ritzy nabe.

Toronto Mayor Olivia Chow called on the community to provide any information about the attack and said there would be added police security around the neighborhood.

“I am deeply troubled by the violent home invasion early this morning in the Bridle Path neighborhood. My thoughts are with the family and their loved ones, who are going through something no family should ever have to face. I am praying for their full recovery,” Chow wrote on X.

The MAC Group is a family-owned company based in Toronto with sub-divisions that specialize in real estate, hospitality and corporate housing.

Morton oversees all divisions of the company as he has 30 years of experience in hospitality and real estate, according to the company’s website.

The couple’s one daughter, Cristina, is listed as the founder of Zohil-Morton law and specializes in Canadian Immigration Law services.

Maggie Zohil-Morton is also listed as an employee for the MAC Group, with her hands on different departments.

TL;DR: This $34.97 Microsoft Office Professional 2021 and Windows 11 Pro bundle (reg. $418.99) combines security and multitasking tools with productivity apps.

A computer can have all the processing power in the world, but that won’t help much if you don’t have the software to get anything done. You still need something to run the machine and something to handle the spreadsheets, presentations, emails, and documents that somehow take up your entire workday. This Microsoft bundle covers both with Windows 11 Pro and Office Professional 2021, available together for a one-time payment of just $34.97 (reg. $418.99).

Windows 11 Pro takes care of the operating system side of things, with features that go beyond the basics. Snap layouts help organize open windows when you’re juggling multiple tasks, while BitLocker encryption adds protection for sensitive files.

If you like getting under the hood of your computer, Hyper-V lets you create virtual machines, and Windows Sandbox provides an isolated space for testing software. You also get support for compatible biometric sign-in hardware and DirectX 12 Ultimate for supported games and graphics cards.

Then there’s Microsoft Office Professional 2021, which includes the apps you’ve probably spent years using. Word handles documents, Excel takes care of spreadsheets, and PowerPoint helps you put together presentations that hopefully don’t require a million slides.

Outlook keeps email and calendars organized, while OneNote is useful for collecting notes and ideas. The package also includes Access, Publisher, and the free version of Teams.

Both licenses are intended for use on one Windows PC, and Office 2021 is tied to the device rather than your Microsoft account. Neither product requires a Microsoft 365 subscription. However, Microsoft ended support for Office 2021 on October 13, 2026, meaning the apps can still run but no longer receive security updates or technical support.

Before purchasing, check that your computer meets Windows 11’s hardware requirements using Microsoft’s PC Health Check app. This license won’t bypass compatibility restrictions, and eligible Windows 10 PCs may already qualify for a free Windows 11 upgrade.

Formerly $418.99, grab the Windows 11 Pro and Microsoft Office Professional 2021 lifetime license bundle for only $34.97.

A round of margaritas turned into a nightmare at a North Carolina Chili’s when bartenders mistakenly mixed a cleaning chemical into customers’ drinks — leaving three customers with chemical burns.

The mix-up happened Wednesday at the restaurant chain’s Forest City location, when an employee preparing the bar for lunch service mistook a granulated degreaser for sugar.

The chemical had been brought to the dining chain two days earlier by a worker who received it from a contractor power-washing the building’s exterior, according to the Foothills Health District.

The substance was placed in an unlabeled container and left in the bar area, where another employee found it Wednesday and mistook it for sugar while preparing margaritas.

Three customers ordered the cocktails and “immediately experienced discomfort,” suffering chemical burns in and around their mouths, the health agency said.

The patrons alerted the restaurant staff before leaving to seek medical attention.

Two employees then tasted the mystery substance in the container and developed similar symptoms.

“I’m not sure what degree of chemical burns they had, but they went to urgent care and were treated there,” Foothills Health District spokesperson Megan Rollins said, according to ABC News13.

The bizarre incident has left at least one regular customer shaken and questioning whether he will return to the restaurant’s bar.

“I was beyond surprised and almost scared,” Chili’s regular Levonne Baker told the outlet.

Baker compared the ordeal to something out of a horror movie.

“It has made me a little nervous about going back to the bar because it’s like what’s in there next? I mean, am I going to be the next person who’s going next door? And not for an oil change,” he said.

A mechanic and an urgent care facility are located next door to the Chili’s.

The Foothills Health District launched an investigation and immediately suspended the restaurant’s food service permit, ordering staff to thoroughly wash and sanitize affected food preparation areas, equipment and surfaces.

The permit was reinstated by Thursday morning after environmental health specialists completed their investigation and determined the restaurant met “all applicable food safety requirements.”

“This incident highlights the importance of proper chemical labeling, storage, and handling in food service establishments, as required by the North Carolina Food Code, to prevent chemical contamination and protect public health,” Foothills Health District Director Jason Masters said.

news.originalContent:
Brent crude prices are up more than 60 percent compared with pre-war levels, despite rebound in supply.

Oil flows out of the Gulf have increased substantially, easing the huge supply disruption caused by the United States/Israel war on Iran.

Crude exports from the Gulf averaged 24.6 million barrels per day (bpd) in the week to October 18, exceeding the pre-war average, according to market intelligence firm Kpler.

Yet, oil prices continue to rise.

Brent crude, the global benchmark, is trading at its highest prices since April, up more than 60 percent compared with before the war.

On Friday, Brent crude front-month futures – contracts for oil deliveries in December – rose more than 2 percent to briefly top $117 a barrel.

The climbing prices reflect anxiety about the possibility of renewed hostilities in the US war on Iran, dwindling oil stocks, and the increased costs of transporting supplies out of the region, according to market analysts.

“The market is doing exactly what it is supposed to do: It is telling us there is plenty of prompt oil, but there is no end to this war in sight – in fact … escalation is very likely,” Adi Imsirovic, a lecturer in energy systems at the University of Oxford, told Al Jazeera.

“Therefore, futures markets reflect that expectation,” Imsirovic, a veteran oil trader, said.

Oil producers have become increasingly adept at responding to the volatile climate in the Middle East to keep supplies flowing.

Facing the threat of Iranian attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, shipping lines have established a shuttle system involving ship-to-ship transfers off Oman and the United Arab Emirates to reduce the distance any one vessel must travel in perilous waters.

Shuttle boats carry the oil through the strait and load it onto waiting tankers once they are out of the danger zone.

In August, more than 70 percent of the crude that crossed the strait did so via ship-to-ship transfers, according to Kpler.

Oil producers have also ramped up exports that bypass the strait altogether via Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline, which carries oil supplies from its eastern oil fields to its Yanbu port on the Red Sea in the west, and the United Arab Emirates’ Habshan-Fujairah pipeline.

As of September, 40 percent of exports from the Gulf were bypassing the strait, a conduit for one-fifth of global oil and liquefied natural gas supplies during peacetime, compared with 17 percent before the war, according to Kpler data.

Such workarounds have nonetheless come at a cost.

Freight costs have reached as much as $40 per barrel in recent weeks, about 10 times the usual rate, according to data from the London Stock Exchange Group, the surge driven by elevated insurance premiums in addition to logistical challenges.

October has been the deadliest month for attacks on commercial vessels since the start of the war, with 32 incidents logged by the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) as of Friday.

“So barrels are moving, but neither smoothly nor reliably. That should not be read as a sign of normalisation,” Isabel Figuerola-Ferretti, an expert in oil markets at Comillas Pontifical University in Madrid, Spain, told Al Jazeera.

“Delivering a barrel has become far more expensive,” Figuerola-Ferretti said.

While market intelligence data has shown exports reaching pre-war levels at various points in recent weeks, the longer-term supply trend is less clear.

Pavel Molchanov, an investment strategist at Raymond James & Associates, expressed scepticism that supply has returned to the pre-conflict trend.

“The IEA’s most recent production data – for September – shows OPEC Gulf production at 15.8 million bpd, which equates to 75 percent of the pre-war baseline,” Molchanov told Al Jazeera, referring to the International Energy Agency’s latest energy outlook.

“That slightly surpassed July’s 74 percent to reach the highest level since the start of the war, but it’s still a considerable distance from 100 percent.”

Meanwhile, oil stockpiles, a buffer during supply disruptions, are waning.

Observed inventories fell by 10 million barrels in September, taking the global stockpile to 509 million barrels below its pre-war level, according to the IEA.

“The market has moved to a chronic squeeze, driven by concrete supply risks: Hormuz transit, shipping and depleted inventories,” Figuerola-Ferretti said.

With no permanent end to the Iran war in sight, few analysts see prices returning to normal anytime soon.

Brent futures for delivery in October 2027 stood at more than $90 a barrel on Friday, in a sign that markets see normality as a long way off, still.

“When could prices return to $70? Not soon,” Figuerola-Ferretti said.

“It would need durable de-escalation, a return to normal transit and shipping conditions through Hormuz, rebuilt inventories and freight costs back to normal,” she added.

Molchanov, the investment strategist, said he did not believe supply could realistically exceed 85 percent of pre-war levels without a permanent diplomatic solution to the war.

“Once the political groundwork is in place, the next steps will be logistical: Demining Hormuz, bringing shipping crews back to work, and resuming production at currently shut-in oilfields,” he said.

See more of our coverage in your search results.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s right-wing bloc won Tuesday’s national election with 53 Knesset seats, ahead of Gadi Eisenkot’s opposition bloc with 48, according to final results published Friday by Israel’s Central Elections Committee.

The result leaves Netanyahu eight seats short of the 61 needed for a governing majority in the 120-member Knesset.

Likud emerged as the largest party with 27 seats, followed by Eisenkot’s Yashar with 21 and Together (B’Yachad) with 12. The Joint List won 11 seats, The Democrats and Ra’am eight each, Yisrael Beiteinu, United Torah Judaism and Otzma Yehudit seven each, and Shas and Religious Zionism six each.

According to the Central Elections Committee, 5,716,665 ballots were cast, for a final turnout of 77.9%. Of those, 5,690,778 were valid and 25,887 invalid.

The electoral threshold of 3.25% was 184,947 votes. All other parties failed to cross it.

The mostly Arab Joint List and Ra’am together won 19 seats, leaving neither of the two Zionist blocs with a majority and setting the stage for difficult coalition negotiations.

Netanyahu hailed Likud’s performance after the vote. “The first thing that has become unequivocally clear is that Likud is the largest party in Israel,” he told supporters.

He called for the establishment of a “strong national right-wing government.”

Eisenkot has also vowed to do all he can to forge a ruling coalition.

“I will do everything in my power to form a Zionist government,” the former IDF chief of staff said.

The final count was announced as the Israeli Security Agency (Shin Bet) continued investigating suspected foreign interference in the election.

Acting Central Elections Committee Director General Dean Livne said the investigation “will not affect the final results submitted to the president,” stressing that it did not concern any particular sector of the population.

The Shin Bet said the inquiry was “focused and limited” and did not cast suspicion on any entire community that had exercised its legal right to vote.

The election committee said the results remain subject to minor corrections during its routine verification process, including checks of polling stations, possible data-entry errors and complaints.

“Subject to minor corrections, as in every election, these are the results that will be submitted to the president of the State of Israel on Wednesday, November 4,” the committee said.

President Isaac Herzog will then hold consultations with representatives of the elected parties before deciding which lawmaker to task with attempting to form the next government.

The 26th Knesset is scheduled to be sworn in on Nov. 10.

news.originalContent:
Pelicans earn first victory over still-winless Kings as Hawks withstand late push to hold off Cavaliers.

Rookie Cameron Boozer recorded 18 points, 12 rebounds and 12 assists for his first career triple-double, and reserve Isaiah Stewart also scored 18 as the Memphis Grizzlies remained unbeaten with a solid 124-103 road victory over the Portland Trail Blazers.

Cedric Coward registered 17 points, seven rebounds and three steals, and Zach Edey added 13 points as Memphis improved to 5-0.

Backup GG Jackson scored 12 points while Ty Jerome, Jaylen Wells and reserve Quinten Post added 10 points apiece for the Grizzlies, who outscored Portland 66-45 in the second half.

Deni Avdija had 24 points, nine rebounds and seven assists to pace the Trail Blazers.

Portland’s Ja Morant had 14 points and three assists in 23 minutes before departing in the fourth quarter due to a left hamstring injury.

Toumani Camara had 13 points and Donovan Clingan added 11 for the Trail Blazers. Damian Lillard had just nine points on 3-of-13 shooting.

A 3-pointer by Jerome gave Memphis a 101-89 advantage with 8:43 left in the contest and started a 13-0 burst. Coward drained a 3-pointer to conclude it and make it 111-89 with 5:31 remaining.

Wells scored on a layup to make it 117-93 with 3:52 left as Memphis cruised to the finish.

The game was tied at halftime but Memphis went on a 12-2 burst in the third quarter with Wells capping it with a 3-pointer to give the Grizzlies a 72-66 lead with 6:13 to play.

Portland later moved within two before Memphis rattled off 10 straight points. Coward culminated the run with a hoop to make it 87-75 with 2:09 remaining.

Lillard drove against former teammate Jerami Grant for a layup with 0.6 seconds left in the third as Portland trailed 91-83 entering the final stanza.

The contest was tied at 58 at halftime when Avdija scored 13 for Portland and Boozer had 13 for Memphis.

Jeremiah Fears flirted with his first career triple-double and the New Orleans Pelicans broke into the win column for the first time this season with a 132-120 triumph over the visiting Sacramento Kings.

Fears and Zion Williamson each scored 22 points for New Orleans. Rookie Darius Acuff Jr poured in a season-best 34 points for Sacramento.

Derik Queen bookended a 12-0 burst early in the second quarter with a 3-pointer and a short jumper, allowing New Orleans to take a 36-32 advantage.

The Kings hung within 67-65 after an Acuff drive to the hoop in the second minute of the third period. But New Orleans then took command for good with a 21-4 flurry, in which Fears and Trey Murphy III drilled consecutive 3-pointers and Williamson contributed six points.

Sacramento still had a chance at 113-106 after a Zach LaVine 3-pointer with 7:11 to play, but New Orleans then ran off the next 10 points before coasting home.

Fears finished with his fourth career double-double, complementing his season-best point total with a career-best 13 assists.

Murphy chipped in with 19 points, Herbert Jones 16, Karlo Matkovic 12, and Saddiq Bey and Ben Mathurin 10 apiece for the Pelicans, who were playing for the second time on a three-game homestand. Williamson had five steals.

De’Andre Hunter and Precious Achiuwa had 24 points apiece, and LaVine totalled 21 for the Kings.

Onyeka Okongwu scored a season-high 29 points, and Nickeil Alexander-Walker sank two crucial free throws with 15.3 seconds remaining as the host Atlanta Hawks snapped a three-game losing streak with a 114-111 victory over the Cleveland Cavaliers.

The Hawks led by 10 with 4:34 remaining, but Cleveland twice pulled within one point, the second time on Donovan Mitchell’s basket with 21 seconds left.

Okongwu went 11-for-17 from the field, including four 3-pointers, and added a season-high 12 rebounds. Alexander-Walker shot 8-for-17 from the field and also made four 3-pointers.

Aaron Wiggins added a season-high 20 points and seven rebounds off the bench, while Jalen Johnson scored 17.

Cleveland got a season-high 24 points from James Harden and 22 points from Mitchell. Sam Merrill came off the bench to make four 3-pointers and score 16.

Cleveland limited the Hawks to 23.8 percent shooting in the first quarter and, prompted by an early 10-3 run, took a 28-16 lead.

The Cavs led 35-24 with 7:22 left in the first half, but Atlanta went on a 13-2 run to tie at 4:33 on a runner by Okongwu. The Hawks took a 46-44 halftime lead.

Atlanta pushed its lead to 61-50 on Alexander-Walker’s 3-pointer with 9:14 left in the third quarter. Cleveland cut the margin to 83-82, fuelled by nine third-quarter points from Harden. Atlanta scored 43 points in the period and entered the fourth quarter with an 89-82 lead.

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

An Australian appeals court on Friday ordered triple-murderer Erin Patterson to never be released from prison because of the “shocking criminality” involved in poisoning four of her estranged husband’s relatives with death cap mushrooms.

The three judges of the Victoria state Court of Appeal dismissed Patterson’s appeal of her convictions and upheld prosecutors’ challenge to the leniency of her 33-year nonparole sentence, meaning she will spend the rest of her life behind bars.

Beforehand, she would have been 82 years old when she could be considered for release.

“This offending was extraordinarily cold and calculated and stands to be denounced in the strongest terms,” Justice Stephen McLeish said on behalf of all three judges.

“In all the circumstances after anxious consideration, we have concluded that the case involved such shocking criminality that it is inappropriate to fix a nonparole period,” McLeish added.

Patterson is only the second woman in Australia to be imprisoned for life without possibility of parole.

The first is meatworker Katherine Knight, who was sentenced in New South Wales state in 2001 for the murder a year earlier of her partner John Price, whom she’d stabbed at least 37 times.

Patterson’s convictions stemmed from a family meal she hosted at her rural home in Leongatha in July 2023.

She can apply to Australia’s High Court to overturn the verdicts on her sentence and her convictions. The High Court is her last appeal option.

Patterson insisted she added death cap mushrooms to the beef Wellington pastry dishes accidentally.

She was sentenced last year to three life sentences for murder and 25 years for attempted murder.

The deaths of Patterson’s parents-in-law Don and Gail Patterson, and Gail’s sister, Heather Wilkinson, within days of having lunch immediately attracted an extraordinary level of global media attention.

The case has also inspired podcasts, books and screen adaptations.

Emmy-nominated actor Melanie Lynskey announced this week she will star as Erin Patterson in a six-episode series for the subscription video-on-demand streaming service Paramount+.

Lynskey is also executive producer of the series that dramatizes the 97 days from the fatal lunch until Patterson’s arrest.

Heather’s husband Ian Wilkinson survived the lunch after spending weeks in hospital. Erin Patterson was convicted of his attempted murder.

Prosecutors argued at an appeal hearing in August that she should never become eligible for parole.

They argued the minimum period behind bars did not reflect the “calculated criminality” of the case.

McLeish said Patterson’s intent to murder all four was sustained for almost three weeks from when she invited them to lunch.

Her crimes involved an “elaborate series of deceptions” including falsely claiming a cancer diagnosis to explain the absences of her two children from the lunch, the judge said.

The only survivor, Ian Wilkinson, testified that Erin Patterson had told her guests she wanted their advice about what to tell the children about her diagnosis.

McLeish noted Erin Patterson had destroyed evidence, denied foraging for mushrooms and repeatedly made false claims about where the mushrooms had come from.

“The offending was carefully planned and deliberate. It represented a cruel breach of trust,” McLeish said.

Patterson opted not to attend court and watched the verdicts by video link from prison.

Because of her notoriety, Patterson is held in the high-security Gordon Unit of Melbourne’s Dame Phyllis Frost Centre women’s prison. The unit is for prisoners assessed as being at high risk from other inmates.

In sentencing her in September 2025, trial judge Christopher Bale said there was a “substantial chance” that Patterson could be held in “solitary confinement for years to come.”

Patterson’s estranged husband, Simon Patterson, was invited to the lunch but declined the day before.

After her conviction, pretrial evidence was released that detailed the husband’s suspicion that Erin Patterson had previously attempted to kill him.

Simon Patterson testified at a pretrial hearing that he had declined the lunch invitation out of fear.
news.content: بیشتر پوشش ما را در نتایج جستجوی خود مشاهده کنید. دادگاه تجدیدنظر استرالیا روز جمعه به ارین پترسون قاتل سه گانه دستور داد که هرگز از زندان آزاد نشود، زیرا "جرمات تکان دهنده" در مسموم کردن چهار تن از بستگان شوهرش با قارچ کلاهک مرگ نقش داشت. سه قاضی دادگاه استیناف ایالت ویکتوریا درخواست تجدیدنظر پترسون در مورد محکومیت‌هایش را رد کردند و اعتراض دادستان‌ها به تخفیف حکم ۳۳ ساله غیر مشروط او را تایید کردند، به این معنی که او بقیه عمر خود را پشت میله‌های زندان سپری می‌کند. پیش از این، او ۸۲ ساله بود که می‌توانست برای آزادی در نظر گرفته شود. قاضی استفان مک لیش به نمایندگی از هر سه قاضی گفت: «این جرم فوق‌العاده سرد و حساب شده بود و باید با شدیدترین عبارات محکوم شود.» مک‌لیش افزود: «در تمام شرایط پس از بررسی نگران‌کننده، به این نتیجه رسیدیم که این پرونده دارای چنان جنایت تکان‌دهنده‌ای است که تعیین دوره عدم آزادی مشروط نامناسب است. پترسون تنها دومین زنی در استرالیا است که بدون امکان آزادی مشروط به حبس ابد محکوم می شود. اولین زنی، کاترین نایت، کارگر گوشت است که در سال 2001 در ایالت نیو ساوت ولز به دلیل قتل شریک زندگی خود جان پرایس، که حداقل 37 ضربه چاقو به او زده بود، محکوم شد. 2023. او می تواند از دادگاه عالی استرالیا درخواست کند تا احکام محکومیت و محکومیت خود را لغو کند. Cou عالی

news.originalContent:
Investigative unit CIR identifies 25 commanders present at five sites during periods of reported sexual violence.

On the day the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) entered el-Fasher in October 2025, a video posted on TikTok showed one of the paramilitary group’s commanders addressing fighters. She appeared to be encouraging fighters to rape women in Sudan’s Northern State, hundreds of kilometres from el-Fasher, the capital of North Darfur.

“The Northern State? You’ll just go for its women, so you cleanse their lineage and bring [brave] sons just like you.”

The speaker was Khademallah Khashmin Herika, also known as Shiraz Khalid, a major commanding the RSF’s female contingent, according to the Centre for Information Resilience (CIR).

The British open-source investigative organisation describes her words as an explicit incitement to rape. It could not establish exactly where the video, posted on October 26, 2025, was filmed. Separate footage placed Herika in el-Fasher and in Garni, where survivors described girls being detained and raped.

Herika is among 25 commanders identified in a CIR investigation into sexual violence in Sudan’s war. Published on Monday, a year after her video was posted, it examines five locations and periods of reported abuse, linking commanders’ appearances and roles to evidence gathered by the United Nations, rights groups and Sudanese organisations.

The findings cover both the RSF and the Sudanese Armed Forces, which have been fighting a three-year-long war, as well as their allied forces. They identify commanders who exercised authority where atrocities were reported, but do not establish that each personally committed or ordered acts of rape.

Investigators checked identities, locations and, where possible, filming dates, with commander sightings independently verified by two analysts. They compared that record with survivor accounts, reported incidents, threatening rhetoric, and indicators of heightened risk, including forced separation of men and women.

The UN fact-finding mission documented mass and gang rape during the RSF takeover of el-Fasher, including at the Saudi Hospital and el-Fasher University. Women and girls were also attacked along escape routes out of the city.

CIR’s report cites a survivor who described being held with other girls at soldiers’ quarters near Garni and raped over two nights. Her family’s detention for ransom further delayed her access to specialist medical care.

The most senior RSF officer identified around el-Fasher was Abdul Rahim Hamdan Dagalo, deputy commander and brother of RSF leader Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo, known as Hemedti.

CIR verified him at the army’s former 6th Infantry Division base on October 26, 2025, and at the Saudi Hospital on November 4.

In separate drone footage from October 27, a voice instructs artillery commander Hussein Abu Jalak to pursue vehicles fleeing an earth embankment outside the city, associated with civilian detention and executions. CIR matched the voice to Dagalo by manually comparing it with other verified recordings of him speaking.

RSF sector commander Gedo Hamdan Ahmed, known as Ibn Shouk, also appears across the investigation: at Zamzam displacement camp during the RSF’s April 2025 assault, then around el-Fasher during its takeover six months later.

His appearances connect two offensives under the same regional command, but they do not establish his responsibility for a specific sexual assault.

Another officer appears on opposing sides of the war.

Abuaqla Mohamed Ahmed Alwakil, known as Kaykal, was appointed commander of an RSF division in Wad Madani on December 19, 2023, according to an RSF announcement cited by CIR.

Investigators verified him at a former army base there on December 24. The same day, the Strategic Initiative for Women in the Horn of Africa documented the rape of seven women at the city’s Industrial School.

The following day, RSF captain Samar Ibrahim Tirab appeared about 750 metres from the school, dismissing reports of rape and looting as lies.

In October 2024, Kaykal defected to the army’s side. When army and allied forces recaptured Wad Madani in January 2025, CIR verified him in the city and nearby Wad al-Mehidi, now commanding the Sudan Shield Forces.

The United Nations human rights office reported that Sudan Shield fighters abducted 13 women and a man from Tayba camp on January 10. Human Rights Watch separately recorded witnesses identifying attackers as Kaykal’s forces. Radio Dabanga reported allegations of rape by the group in Tayba and other settlements.

In Gezira, southeast of Khartoum, CIR also examined abuses against Kanabi communities, historically marginalised settlements made up of descendants of migrant agricultural workers. These communities faced attacks amid accusations of supporting the RSF.

Verified footage from Hantoub Bridge shows fighters beating and sexually degrading a detained man before pushing him off the bridge. CIR identified insignia associated with the army-allied Baraa Bin Malik Brigade, General Intelligence Service and Special Mission Forces.

The most senior army officer CIR placed in Wad Madani during the recapture was Major-General Abdelmoneim Abdelbasit Mohamed, commander of the Sennar axis, identified on January 12, 2025.

His presence is part of CIR’s assessment of command structures, but it does not establish that he directed the filmed attack.

Al Jazeera contacted the RSF and the Sudanese Armed Forces to ask for a response to the findings laid out in this article, but received no response.

Both the RSF and the Sudanese Armed Forces have previously denied allegations of sexual violence by their personnel.

On October 26, Britain imposed sanctions on 15 senior commanders from Sudan’s rival forces over suspected atrocities, including conflict-related sexual violence.

The measures include asset freezes and travel bans. Among those named were Abu Jalak and Al-Nour Ahmed Adam, known as al-Qubba, whom the UK Foreign Office linked to the siege and assault on el-Fasher.

The UK government said the announcement followed CIR reporting on sexual violence and starvation. It also pledged 5 million pounds ($6.7m) for survivors, including healthcare and psychosocial support, and a further 10 million pounds ($13.4m) for humanitarian assistance.

The 15 sanctions designations are a separate list from the 25 commanders cited in CIR’s report, and sanctions do not equate to criminal convictions.

CIR says it has reasonable grounds to believe the commanders identified were directly or indirectly responsible for sexual violence. It also explicitly states that data limitations prevent it from attributing individual responsibility for specific incidents.

Presence, rank and repeated appearances can guide further investigation; but they cannot alone establish criminal guilt. A command-responsibility case would also require evidence about effective control, knowledge and failures to take necessary measures to prevent, repress or report crimes.

For survivors, stigma, insecurity and inaccessible services still obstruct both treatment and testimony. The investigation preserves another source of evidence: the images fighters recorded themselves.
news.content:
واحد تحقیق CIR 25 فرمانده حاضر در پنج سایت را در دوره‌های خشونت جنسی گزارش شده شناسایی می‌کند. در روزی که نیروهای پشتیبانی سریع (RSF) در اکتبر 2025 وارد الفاشر شدند، ویدئویی که در TikTok منتشر شد یکی از فرماندهان گروه شبه‌نظامی را نشان می‌دهد که با جنگجویان صحبت می‌کند. به نظر می رسید که او جنگجویان را تشویق می کند که به زنان در ایالت شمالی سودان، صدها کیلومتر از الفاشر، پایتخت دارفور شمالی، تجاوز کنند. "ایالت شمالی؟ شما فقط به دنبال زنان آن خواهید رفت، بنابراین نسب آنها را پاک می کنید و پسران [شجاع] مانند خود را می آورید."
به گفته مرکز تاب آوری اطلاعات (CIR) سخنران خادم الله خشمین هریکا، معروف به شیراز خالد، سرگرد فرمانده گروه زنان RSF بود. سازمان تحقیقاتی منبع باز بریتانیا سخنان او را به عنوان تحریک صریح به تجاوز توصیف می کند. نمی‌توان دقیقاً محل فیلم‌برداری این ویدیو را که در 26 اکتبر 2025 ارسال شده بود، مشخص کرد. فیلم‌های جداگانه هریکا را در الفاشر و گارنی نشان می‌دهد، جایی که بازماندگان دخترانی را توصیف می‌کنند که بازداشت و مورد تجاوز جنسی قرار گرفته‌اند. هریکا یکی از 25 فرماندهی است که در تحقیقات CIR در مورد خشونت جنسی در جنگ سودان شناسایی شده‌اند. این ویدئو که روز دوشنبه، یک سال پس از انتشار ویدئوی او منتشر شد، به بررسی پنج مکان و دوره‌های سوء استفاده گزارش‌شده می‌پردازد و ظاهر و نقش فرماندهان را به شواهد جمع‌آوری‌شده توسط سازمان ملل، گروه‌های حقوق بشر و سازمان‌های سودانی مرتبط می‌کند. یافته‌ها هم نیروهای RSF و هم نیروهای مسلح سودان را شامل می‌شود که سه سال درگیر جنگ بوده‌اند.

news.originalContent:
Persistent wildfires sparked by drought have enveloped the region in smog.

Toxic smoke from wildfires killed 3,560 people in Indonesia last month, according to a new report.

The study, released by the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA) on Thursday, found that air pollution-related deaths in Indonesia surged by 42 percent in September, rising from an estimated 3,740 people killed in August to 5,310.

Toxic smoke from forest and land fires caused 3,560 deaths last month, the report said. “Chronic, non-fire emissions from urban and industrial air pollution sources” caused another 1,750 deaths, the Helsinki-based think tank found.

Toxic fire smoke accounted for 94-99 percent of air pollution-related deaths in Kalimantan, on the island of Borneo, and more than 80 percent on Sumatra, the regions worst affected by the fires, the report notes.

Deaths on the southern island of Java, meanwhile, remained largely tied to urban and industrial sources, the study found.

It added that the number of citizens exposed to “unhealthy” to “hazardous” air quality reached a record peak of 58 million in September.

“Citizens inhaling hazardous-level air in Kalimantan alone nearly tripled from 2.8 million to 6.4 million during the worst days of the month,” it found.

Amid an El Nino weather pattern, Indonesia has been dealing with devastating wildfires sparked by severe drought, which have led to deforestation and sent toxic smog across the Southeast Asian archipelago.

It has also raised pollution levels in neighbouring countries, including Malaysia, Singapore, the Philippines and East Timor.

The government in Jakarta is facing increasing criticism for its response to the fires. On Wednesday, it defended its approach, noting it has deployed more than 72,000 people to carry out cloud-seeding and firefighting operations, activated more than 2,100 doctors and health workers in hard-hit areas, and distributed 5.3 million masks.
news.content: آتش سوزی های مداوم ناشی از خشکسالی منطقه را در دود فراگرفته است. طبق یک گزارش جدید، دود سمی ناشی از آتش سوزی های جنگلی در ماه گذشته 3560 نفر را در اندونزی کشت. این مطالعه که توسط مرکز تحقیقات انرژی و هوای پاک (CREA) در روز پنجشنبه منتشر شد، نشان داد که مرگ و میر ناشی از آلودگی هوا در اندونزی 7 درصد افزایش یافته است. در ماه اوت به 5310 رسید. بر اساس این گزارش، دود سمی ناشی از آتش‌سوزی‌های جنگلی و زمینی در ماه گذشته باعث مرگ 3560 نفر شد. اندیشکده مستقر در هلسینکی دریافت که "انتشارهای مزمن و غیر آتش سوزی از منابع آلودگی هوای شهری و صنعتی" باعث 1750 مرگ دیگر شده است. دود آتش سمی عامل 94 تا 99 درصد مرگ و میر ناشی از آلودگی هوا در کالیمانتان، در جزیره بورنئو، و بیش از 80 درصد در مناطقی که آتش سوزی در سوماترا تحت تاثیر قرار نمی گیرد، بوده است. در همین حال، این مطالعه نشان داد که مرگ و میر در جزیره جنوبی جاوه تا حد زیادی به منابع شهری و صنعتی وابسته است. این مطالعه اضافه کرد که تعداد شهروندانی که در معرض کیفیت هوای "ناسالم" تا "خطرناک" قرار گرفتند به رکورد 58 میلیون نفر در سپتامبر رسید. بدترین روزهای ماه. در میان الگوی آب و هوای ال نینو، اندونزی با آتش‌سوزی‌های ویرانگر ناشی از خشکسالی شدید مواجه شده است که منجر به جنگل‌زدایی و انتشار دود سمی در سراسر مجمع‌الجزایر آسیای جنوب شرقی شده است.

news.originalContent:
Holders Man City will take on Bradford City, Crystal Palace will welcome Sunderland, while Bournemouth play Liverpool.

Everton advanced to the League Cup quarterfinals with a 3-1 victory over Newcastle United, setting up a clash against fourth-tier side Fleetwood Town.

First-half goals from James Garner and Hayden Hackney put the hosts in control before Thierno Barry struck after the break at the Hill Dickinson Stadium, with Dan Burn scoring late for the visitors on Thursday.

The Merseyside club eased through despite the absence of midfielder Jack Grealish, who was dropped from the squad following an internal breach of club discipline. Prime Minister Andy Burnham, an Everton supporter, was among the crowd.

Everton will travel to League Two side Fleetwood, who stunned Premier League champions Arsenal on Tuesday. Mikel Arteta’s side crashed out 5-3 on penalties in an incredible fourth-round upset after the tie finished 1-1 in normal time.

Crystal Palace will welcome Sunderland, while Bournemouth will play away at Liverpool, who beat Chelsea 6-5 in a dramatic penalty shootout on Wednesday.

Defending champions Manchester City will take on third-tier side Bradford City. They avoided the fate that befell Arsenal and stayed on course to retain their title by twice coming from behind to draw 2-2 against Brighton, then triumph 4-3 in the shootout.

The quarterfinals are scheduled to take place in the week beginning December 14.
news.content: دارندگان من سیتی به مصاف برادفورد سیتی می‌روند، کریستال پالاس از ساندرلند استقبال می‌کند، در حالی که بورنموث با لیورپول بازی می‌کند. اورتون با پیروزی 3-1 مقابل نیوکاسل یونایتد به مرحله یک چهارم نهایی جام اتحادیه صعود کرد و درگیری را با تیم رده چهارمی فلیت‌وود تاون ترتیب داد. گل‌های نیمه اول جیمز گارنر و هیدن هاکنی قبل از اینکه تیرنو بری بعد از استراحت در ورزشگاه هیل دیکنسون ضربه ای بزند، میزبان را کنترل کرد. دن برن در روز پنجشنبه دیر برای میهمان گلزنی کرد. اندی برنهام، نخست وزیر، یکی از هواداران اورتون، در میان جمعیت بود. اورتون به تیم لیگ دو فلیت وود سفر خواهد کرد که روز سه شنبه آرسنال قهرمان لیگ برتر را شگفت زده کرد. تیم میکل آرتتا در ضربات پنالتی 5-3 در یک شکست باورنکردنی دور چهارم پس از پایان تساوی 1-1 در زمان عادی شکست خورد. کریستال پالاس از ساندرلند استقبال خواهد کرد، در حالی که بورنموث در خارج از خانه مقابل لیورپول بازی خواهد کرد که در ضربات پنالتی دراماتیک روز چهارشنبه چلسی را 6-5 شکست داد. منچسترسیتی مدافع عنوان قهرمانی به مصاف تیم دسته سومی بردفورد سیتی خواهد رفت. آنها از سرنوشتی که برای آرسنال رخ داد اجتناب کردند و با دو بار تساوی 2-2 مقابل برایتون، در مسیر حفظ عنوان خود ماندند، سپس در ضربات بازی 4-3 پیروز شدند. مرحله یک چهارم نهایی قرار است در هفته ای که از 14 دسامبر شروع می شود برگزار شود.

news.originalContent:
Kenya aims to turn its rich athletics heritage into a lasting legacy for the continent.

Nairobi, Kenya – For more than four decades, the World Athletics Championships have been held across continents but never in Africa.

That changes in 2029, when Nairobi becomes the first African city to host the track and field championships, bringing the sport’s flagship global competition to a continent whose athletes have helped shape its history.

The World Athletics Championships were established in 1983 in Helsinki, Finland, after decades in which athletics’ biggest global competitions were largely tied to the Olympic Games. The inaugural championships brought together 1,333 athletes from 153 countries, laying the foundation for one of the most important events on the international sporting calendar.

Africa’s relationship with athletics stretches much further back. Ethiopia’s Abebe Bikila became the first African to win Olympic marathon gold in 1960, followed by generations of track and field athletes including Uganda’s John Akii-Bua, Morocco’s Said Aouita and a succession of Kenyan champions.

Kenya’s own story is particularly significant. Kipchoge Keino’s 1,500-metre triumph at the 1968 Mexico City Olympics helped establish Kenya as a global distance-running powerhouse. Generations that followed – from Paul Tergat and David Rudisha to Eliud Kipchoge, Vivian Cheruiyot, Hellen Obiri and Faith Kipyegon – have turned Kenyan athletics into a global sporting identity.

Kenya is the second most successful nation in World Athletics Championships history.

For Keino, the two-time Olympic champion and former world record holder whose achievements helped establish Kenya’s reputation in distance running, Nairobi’s selection represents the culmination of decades of progress.

“When we started running, we were young Kenyans with a dream to represent our country and show the world that African athletes could compete at the highest level. Seeing Kenya prepare to host the World Athletics Championships in 2029 is a deeply special moment,” Keino told Al Jazeera.

“It is a testament to how far our country has come from sending athletes abroad to compete, to welcoming the world to our own home.”

Keino said hosting the championships would also give Kenya an opportunity to showcase its talent, culture and hospitality while investing in the future of athletics.

Kenya’s campaign to host the 2029 championships lasted three years and culminated in victory at the World Athletics Council meeting in Budapest on September 15 .

Competing bids came from London, Rome and Munich, all cities with established records of hosting major international athletics events.

Nairobi’s bid highlighted the ongoing renovation of Kasarani stadium ahead of the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations, as well as Kenya’s experience hosting the 2017 World U18 Championships and the 2021 World U20 junior Championships. Kenya also drew lessons from its unsuccessful bid for the 2025 championships, which was awarded to Tokyo.

World Athletics President Sebastian Coe said the council had received four strong bids and described Nairobi’s proposal as “compelling and emotional”.

“Nairobi and Munich ultimately presented two compelling propositions. They offer very different but equally exciting opportunities for our sport, and I am delighted that we can now begin working with both cities to stage two world-class championships,” Coe said.

Athletics Kenya declined to comment on the decision.

The celebrations were quickly accompanied by questions over whether Kenya can host an event of this scale while dealing with persistent scrutiny over doping in athletics.

Since the international sport governing body World Athletics established the Athletics Integrity Unit in 2017, 318 Kenyan athletes have been sanctioned for anti-doping rule violations, according to figures reported following the announcement. Of those, 136 were still serving bans.

Kenya is not among the countries with the highest overall number of anti-doping violations globally, but its prominence in distance running means high-profile cases often attract considerable international attention.

Kenya’s anti-doping system has also faced scrutiny. In 2025, the World Anti-Doping Agency found Kenya’s anti-doping agency non-compliant with the global anti-doping code, putting additional scrutiny on the country’s system. Kenya was removed from the agency’s compliance watchlist in 2026 after corrective measures.

Recent cases, including the bans of marathon world-record holder Ruth Chepngetich and former half-marathon world-record holder Kibiwott Kandie, have kept the issue in the spotlight.

For Nairobi, the challenge will be to demonstrate that its anti-doping systems are strong enough to protect the credibility of the 2029 championships.

Kenyan Member of Parliament Dan Wanyama, who chairs the committee on sports and culture, said the country has the experience and infrastructure to host the event.

“We have already held several athletics championships which were very successful. It is a thing of pride for us to defeat major global cities London, Munich and Rome,” Wanyama told Al Jazeera.

“As the chair of the sports committee in Parliament, I can assure you we have the right infrastructure in place because the championship will be held at Moi International Sports Stadium (known locally as Kasarani). The contractor is already on site and preparations have started in earnest.”

Kenyan athletics fan Winston Omondi said some of the criticism of Kenya was unfairly focused on the country.

“If it was about doping, then there are so many developed countries that should not even be participating in athletics, including London itself,” Omondi told Al Jazeera.

Doping is not the only test facing Kenya.

As the country prepares to host the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations with sporting infrastructure being upgraded at Kasarani and Nyayo stadiums, the World Athletics Championships will require more than a competition venue.

Nairobi will have to ensure adequate training and warm-up facilities while improving transport links, accommodation and athlete services. The city will also need reliable systems for security, accreditation, broadcasting, medical care and the movement of thousands of athletes, officials, journalists and spectators.

Beyond the stadiums, Nairobi’s wider infrastructure will come under scrutiny, particularly its traffic congestion and public transport network.

The success of the championships will therefore depend on more than upgrading Kasarani. Kenya will have to demonstrate that Nairobi can deliver a seamless experience for a global sporting event while maintaining the standards expected of one of athletics’ biggest competitions.

For a country whose athletes have spent decades representing Africa on the world stage, hosting the championships is a historic opportunity. It is also a test of whether a continent that has produced generations of world-class athletes can host the sport’s biggest global events on its own ground.

But winning the bid was only the first race.

As Omondi put it: “We have come so far as people, as a country and as a continent for us to be judged in this way.”
news.content: کنیا قصد دارد میراث غنی دو و میدانی خود را به میراثی ماندگار برای این قاره تبدیل کند. نایروبی، کنیا - بیش از چهار دهه است که مسابقات جهانی دو و میدانی در سراسر قاره‌ها برگزار می‌شود اما هرگز در آفریقا برگزار نمی‌شود. این در سال 2029 تغییر می‌کند، زمانی که نایروبی به اولین شهر آفریقایی تبدیل می‌شود که میزبان رقابت‌های دوومیدانی جهانی می‌شود. ورزشکاران به شکل گیری تاریخ آن کمک کرده اند. مسابقات جهانی دو و میدانی در سال 1983 در هلسینکی، فنلاند، پس از دهه‌ها که بزرگترین رقابت‌های جهانی دو و میدانی عمدتاً با بازی‌های المپیک مرتبط بود، تأسیس شد. مسابقات قهرمانی افتتاحیه 1333 ورزشکار از 153 کشور را گرد هم آورد و پایه و اساس یکی از مهم ترین رویدادهای تقویم ورزشی بین المللی را گذاشت. رابطه آفریقا با دو و میدانی بسیار دورتر است. آببه بیکیلا از اتیوپی اولین آفریقایی شد که طلای ماراتن المپیک را در سال 1960 به دست آورد و به دنبال آن نسل‌های ورزشکار دوومیدانی از جمله جان آکی بوآ از اوگاندا، سعید آویتا از مراکش و تعدادی از قهرمانان کنیایی به دست آوردند. داستان خود کنیا به ویژه قابل توجه است. قهرمانی کیپچوگه کینو در 1500 متر در المپیک 1968 مکزیکو سیتی به ایجاد کنیا به عنوان یک نیروگاه جهانی برای دویدن مسافت کمک کرد. نسل‌های بعدی - از پل ترگات و دیوید رودیشا گرفته تا الیود کیپچوگه، ویویان چرویوت، هلن اوبیری و فیث کیپیگون - دو و میدانی کنیایی را به یک هویت ورزشی جهانی تبدیل کردند. کنیا دومین

news.originalContent:
Hamed Mirzaei lost his wife, parents and many others in a devastating US-Israeli attack on Tehran.

Hamed Mirzaei lost 12 members of his family in an attack on a residential building in Tehran. Among those killed was his wife, 26-year-old Mohadeseh. The young couple had been planning to start a family.

He describes how the United States-Israeli attack on his home on March 9, 2026, changed his life in this first-person account, shared with Al Jazeera:

“Seven months have passed since the bombing. Even now, on many days, when I come to my senses, I find myself back at my destroyed home, searching for my loved ones.

“My grandfather and my father’s uncle built the house that was hit. They divided its apartments among their children. A year ago, when I got married, my wife and I moved into one of the apartments in the same building. We were just beginning to prepare for a child. We were young, with our whole lives ahead of us. Then the bombing happened.

“March 9 was a Monday. At about 1:00 in the afternoon, I left home to check in at work. At 2:30 pm, my wife messaged me, asking me to buy her some headache medicine on my way back. I called her to ask which medicine she wanted, but her phone was busy. We were expecting guests at home, so I called our guest’s phone. That line was busy, too. I hung up, intending to call my wife again.

“I was five minutes from home when I suddenly heard a whistling sound. The first missile had just struck.

“The ground shook beneath my feet from the force of the explosion. With my phone still in my hand, I called my wife again, but her phone was unreachable. I began calling my family members, my grandfather, my father, my mother. All their phones were unreachable.

“Even so, I thought our home had not been hit. I kept telling myself it was impossible that they had struck our house. I thought perhaps a missile had hit somewhere else in our neighbourhood. In those moments, all I wanted was to get home and see that the house was still standing.

“In those same minutes, five more missiles struck our home.

“When I arrived, I saw that everyone in the neighbourhood had come out of their homes, but I still couldn’t bring myself to step into the street. It never even crossed my mind that those missiles could have hit our house. But they had. Even from a distance, it was clear that all that remained of the house was its skeleton.

“When I reached it, everything was burning. All I could think about was getting to the second floor and finding my wife, but the staircase was gone. Several neighbours from the first floor were trapped beneath the rubble. The Red Crescent helped rescue them.

“I thought that if they kept searching, perhaps they would find my family alive somewhere beneath the debris, too. But they didn’t. No one was found that hour. Nor in the hours that followed. By nightfall, no one else had been found in the building. Twelve members of my family were missing, and I still couldn’t bring myself to leave.

“That night, the next day, the day after that, and every day following the attack, I returned to my home. For 20 days, I searched through the rubble and the remnants of the missiles and explosions for my loved ones. There was nothing left.

“My wife was killed. My sister-in-law, who had been a guest in our home, was killed. My father and mother, my grandfather and grandmother, my aunt’s husband and her daughter, my uncle, my father’s cousin, his wife and their child were all killed. Twelve members of my family died in the attack, and people ask me how I am.

“I miss them. I miss them more with every passing day. At first, I thought that perhaps, with time, our grief would ease and we would find some peace. But we haven’t. As each day passes, I feel worse.

“I was an only child, and I always thought that, although I had no brothers or sisters, I had a large family with whom I would grow old. All my life, the members of our extended family had lived together, side by side. Now all those people, and all the love that flowed through our family, have vanished.

“I am the only one left. There is no one else from my family. I am utterly alone.

“I am living proof for anyone who still believes that war can lead to a good outcome. Anyone who thinks war is good should look at what has happened to me and ask themselves: ‘What, in any of this, is good?’

“The building where I was born, the building where my father was born, the building where I had hoped my child would be born, all of it was destroyed in a fraction of a second. My home and my family were wiped out together. And when I miss them, I truly don’t know where to turn or what to look at.

“Seven months have passed since the day they destroyed our home, and every day, when I wake up, I come here to look at the ruins. I cannot bring myself to leave this place. I feel as though my life is buried here, and I return every day, hoping I might find some piece of it. But there is nothing left.

“When someone asks me what I am thinking or how I feel, I cannot answer. Everything I have ever done in my life was for the happiness of my family. Now I no longer have a family for whom I can do anything.

“Every day, I ask myself: ‘Why do I keep going?’ I have no answer.

“The difference between me and my family, who were killed, is that they were buried beneath the rubble, while I am still walking around. Other than that, I am just as dead as they are. The only difference is that my name is not included among the dead.”
news.content:
حامد میرزایی همسر، والدین و بسیاری دیگر را در حمله ویرانگر آمریکا و اسرائیل به تهران از دست داد. حامد میرزایی 12 نفر از اعضای خانواده خود را در حمله به یک ساختمان مسکونی در تهران از دست داد. در میان کشته شدگان همسرش محدثه 26 ساله نیز دیده می شود. این زوج جوان قصد تشکیل خانواده را داشتند. او توضیح می دهد که چگونه حمله ایالات متحده و اسرائیل به خانه اش در 9 مارس 2026 زندگی او را تغییر داد در این حساب اول شخص که با الجزیره به اشتراک گذاشته شده است:
"هفت ماه از بمباران می گذرد. حتی اکنون، بسیاری از روزها، وقتی به خودم می آیم، خود را در خانه ویران شده ام می بینم و به دنبال عزیزانم می گردم." پدربزرگم و عموی پدرم خانه ای را که مورد اصابت قرار گرفته بود ساختند. آپارتمان های آن را بین فرزندانشان تقسیم کردند. یک سال پیش که ازدواج کردم، من و همسرم به یکی از آپارتمان های همان ساختمان نقل مکان کردیم. تازه داشتیم برای بچه آماده شدن. ما جوان بودیم و تمام زندگی‌مان در پیش بود. سپس بمباران اتفاق افتاد. «9 مارس دوشنبه بود. حدود ساعت 1 بعد از ظهر از خانه خارج شدم تا در محل کار خود را بررسی کنم. ساعت 2:30 بعد از ظهر همسرم به من پیام داد و از من خواست در راه بازگشت برایش داروی سردرد بخرم. زنگ زدم بهش بپرسم کدوم دارو می خوای ولی گوشیش شلوغ بود. ما در خانه منتظر مهمان بودیم، بنابراین با تلفن مهمانمان تماس گرفتم. اون خط هم شلوغ بود تماس را قطع کردم و قصد داشتم دوباره به همسرم زنگ بزنم. "پنج دقیقه از خانه دور بودم که ناگهان صدای سوت شنیدم. اولین موشک تازه اصابت کرده بود."
